newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest power shoot higher as cold bites deep.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest power shoot higher as cold bites deep.

text.p: Wholesale spot electricity prices for the U.S. Midwest were higher again Wednesday, propped up by a cold front in the area and natural gas prices approaching the $5 mark, sources said.
Temperatures throughout most of the Midwest are expected to be much below normal through Saturday but then begin to moderate by Sunday.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power prices for Thursday delivery were in the $41.00-43.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, up from Tuesday's $28.00-31.00 trading range.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power deals were assessed higher at $16.00-17.00.
January peak MAPP prices were talked around $23.50.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Thursday delivery were also higher in the $39.00-41.00 range, up from the $30.00-32.00 trades seen on Tuesday.
MAIN off peak power was notionally assessed in the $15.00-16.00 range.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Thursday firmed into the $36.00-37.00 range early and then as high as $47.00 late.
Traders said most deals were done at the lower end of the range, up from Tuesday's $28.00-30.00 trading range.
January/February ECAR prices were steady in the $25.30-26.00 range, while March business was talked in the $21.40-22.00 area.
Off-peak, non-firm next-day ECAR power was notionally talked again in the $15.00-16.00 range.
"More people are concentrating on hourly stuff. There really isn't any off-peak market," one trader said.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), peak non-firm power for Thursday was quoted mostly around $40 per MWh, up about $10 from Wednesday.
January/February peak prices in SPP were talked in the $27.60-28.50 range, down slightly from Wednesday.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were notionally around at $14.00-17.00.
Kansas City Power and Light Co's 670 megawatt (MW) Iatan coal-fired unit, shut early Tuesday, is expected to return to service early Thursday, the company said.
Also, Omaha Public Service's 585 MW coal-fired unit in Nebraska City, Neb., is expected to resume operating early Friday.

Contributing to the stronger electricity prices were the higher, but volatile, natural gas prices. In the Midcontinent, gas for Thursday delivery traded anywhere from $4.70 to about $4.95, with the bulk of the deals done in the low-$4.70s.
